Our technology combines precision positioning, software, and automated field equipment to simplify repetitive tasks and help customers get more done on their job sites. As we grow our presence in Texas, we’re building a local support operation to provide customers with accessible training, responsive technical support, and reliable equipment. About the Role We’re looking for a Geospatial Support & Operations Manager to help build our Houston support operation. You’ll be a go-to resource for customers, helping them get started with our systems, understand the right workflows, troubleshoot day-to-day issues, and use our technology confidently in the field. This role combines geospatial product knowledge, customer training and support, and day-to-day operational ownership. Alongside supporting customers remotely and on-site, you’ll coordinate equipment readiness, inventory, shipments, returns, and replacements. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys helping customers adopt technical products and taking ownership of a local operation as it grows. What You’ll Do Own day-to-day customer support. Help customers resolve questions and issues related to system setup, positioning, software workflows, and equipment use. Keep customers informed and follow issues through to resolution. Deliver customer training and onboarding. Train operators and customer teams remotely and at job sites, explaining how to set up, operate, and troubleshoot our systems in their daily work. Apply geospatial knowledge in the field. Help customers understand how our technology fits into their surveying, positioning, and construction-layout workflows, and identify setup or operational issues that affect successful use. Coordinate advanced support and equipment replacements. Gather clear information about issues, document troubleshooting steps, and escalate mechanical or advanced technical problems to Engineering and Level 2 support. Arrange swaps or replacements when appropriate. Run the local support operation. Maintain organized equipment and inventory records, track available and returned units, and coordinate shipping, receiving, and customer deployment needs. Maintain equipment readiness and quality. Perform standard setup, functionality, and readiness checks using established procedures before equipment is shipped or provided to customers. Improve support processes and documentation. Maintain support records, develop practical troubleshooting guides and training materials, and help establish consistent operating procedures for the Houston location. Partner across the business. Work with Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and Engineering to support customer handoffs, equip customer-facing teammates to handle routine field tasks, and share feedback that improves our products and service. What We’re Looking For Relevant experience with geospatial technology, surveying, GNSS/GPS positioning, construction layout, machine control, or closely related technical products. Experience providing customer-facing technical support, product training, applications support, or equipment onboarding. The ability to troubleshoot systematically, distinguish setup or user-workflow issues from problems requiring advanced support, and communicate clear findings to the right team. Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts to customers with different levels of experience. Excellent organization and follow-through, with the ability to manage support requests, equipment readiness, inventory, and daily operational priorities. A practical, service-oriented approach: comfortable working independently, supporting customers under pressure, and taking ownership without needing a rigid process for every situation. Willingness to work on-site in Houston and travel to customer locations for training and support, with a valid driver’s license. ﻿ What You’ll Get A high-impact role in a fast-growing robotics startup. Our mission is to bridge the workforce gap and accelerate the development of critical infrastructure projects with cutting-edge robotics and autonomous navigation technology. With over 100 robots deployed and actively transforming construction sites worldwide, we’re redefining efficiency, safety, and precision in the field. Backed by top-tier investors, Civ Robotics is a fast-growing startup headquartered in San Francisco, founded by industry experts with deep construction experience. Join us in building the future of construction automation and be part of a team that’s shaping the next generation of robotics. About the Role We’re hiring a Sales Engineer to join our Sales team and serve as a technical leader across the customer lifecycle, from pre-sales demos and technical discovery through deployments, training, adoption, and expansion support. You’ll partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and Engineering to help customers successfully adopt Civ Robotics in real-world construction environments. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving hands-on technical challenges, building trust with customers, and driving outcomes that directly impact revenue and retention. This role is for someone based on the Mid West and requires regular travel to customer job sites. What You’ll Do Pre-Sales / Technical Selling Lead technical discovery to understand customer workflows, constraints, and success criteria. Run compelling product demos (office + on-site) and communicate value in a practical, customer-specific way. Partner with Sales on evaluations, pilots, proposals, and technical validation to support closing and expansion. Serve as a trusted technical advisor to stakeholders across operations, site leadership, technical teams, and executives. Comfort working with metrics and customer health signals (adoption, retention risk, ROI). What You’ll Get A high-impact role in a fast-growing robotics startup. jobs.title: Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer
jobs.description: View all jobs Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer San Francisco Engineering In office Full-time About the Company Civ Robotics is on a mission to automate repetitive tasks within the $3 trillion infrastructure construction industry. We’re dedicated to bridging the workforce gap and accelerating the development of essential infrastructure projects. At the core of our mission is our innovative technology in robotics and autonomous navigation. With over 100 robots deployed and operating across construction sites worldwide, we pride ourselves in ushering in the next generation of construction layout tools for solar, civil, land surveying, road striping, and general contracting. Our technology is engineered from the ground up to make our customers’ projects more precise, simple, and efficient than ever before. Join us and become an integral member of our dynamic team, leading the charge in pioneering construction robotics innovation! About the Role We are seeking a Quality Assurance Engineer to own and continuously improve the testing and validation of our robotics products. You will test the complete system, including Android applications, robotics software, hardware integrations, cloud services, and autonomous workflows. The role combines hands-on testing with test automation and requires thinking beyond individual software features to validate how the entire robotic system behaves in real-world scenarios. You will work closely with robotics, software, hardware, product, and field teams to identify issues early, improve product reliability, and ensure every release is ready for deployment. Key Responsibilities Develop and execute test plans and test cases for robotics products and applications. Perform functional, regression, integration, system, and end-to-end testing. Build and maintain automated testing infrastructure and test workflows. Test Android applications used to operate and configure robotic systems. Validate complete workflows such as robot connection, mission loading, operation, stopping, reporting, and configuration. Run tests using HITL/simulation environments as well as physical robotic systems. Develop and maintain long-running reliability and endurance tests, including overnight and multi-hour operation. Perform exploratory and randomized testing to identify unexpected failures and edge cases. Validate new features and releases and ensure existing functionality is not affected. Reproduce, document, and track issues with clear steps, logs, and supporting data. Collaborate with engineering teams to investigate failures and verify fixes. Continuously improve testing processes, automation coverage, and release quality. Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field. Experience: 3+ years of professional experience in software QA, test automation, system testing, or a related role. Technical Skills Strong experience with software testing methodologies and test automation. Experience testing complex systems involving multiple software and hardware components. Experience developing automated tests using Python or similar scripting languages. Experience with Android application testing. Experience with API and integration testing. Comfortable working with Linux and command-line tools. Ability to analyze logs, system behavior, and failures across multiple components. Familiarity with Git, JIRA, and CI/CD pipelines. Strong understanding of regression testing, release validation, and defect management. Soft Skills Strong problem-solving and debugging abilities. Exceptional attention to detail. Ability to think creatively about how systems can fail. Strong ownership mindset and commitment to product quality. Ability to work collaboratively in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. Clear written and verbal communication. Preferred Qualifications Experience testing robotics or autonomous systems. Familiarity with ROS/ROS2. Experience with simulation, SIL, or HITL testing. Experience testing systems combining mobile apps, cloud services, embedded software, sensors, and robotics. Experience building automated or agentic testing systems. Familiarity with long-duration, stress, reliability, and fault-injection testing. Experience with Docker and containerized environments. Experience working with hardware or robots in the field. Why Join Us Work on cutting-edge robotics technology deployed on real construction sites. Own quality across the complete robotics stack, from applications and cloud services to autonomous machines. Join a tight-knit, multidisciplinary team with significant ownership and fast decision cycles. Help shape the testing infrastructure and quality processes of a rapidly growing robotics company. Benefits & Perks Comprehensive healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) for you and your family. Competitive salary with growth potential. Equity options in a fast-growing robotics company. jobs.title: Solar Farms
jobs.description: Solar Farms Solar farms represent the peak of renewable energy innovation. Solar farms' layout plays an important role because of their massive scale, often spanning vast areas with hundreds of thousands of points to survey and plan. Civ Robotics in solar farms The CivDot and CivDot+ are engineered to automate and redefine surveying in the solar landscape. With these autonomous robots, installers have increased the layout output by 8x and reduced costs by more than 50%. From precise pre-drilling, pilling, and staging piles to installing fences, MV lines, and energy storage facilities, the robots are optimizing numerous aspects of solar farm development. What you lay out is what you build! Piling Piling involves driving I beams into the ground to provide stability and support for suspended solar panels. Civ Robotics' GPS-equipped surveying robots help the crew swiftly identify where to pound the piles in the ground. It’s important that each pile is placed in the right spot with no room for error to ensure all solar arrays are aligned. CivDot+ is a great tool for pile layout alongside standard pile drivers. Even with a GPS-enabled pile driver, marking the pile coordinates has many benefits: Avoid looking at the screen while driving Improve worker safety Increase piling productivity by 10% Double verify pile position and type Staging Piles (Shakeout) Staging in solar farms involves distributing piles close enough to the pile coordinate before piling. The process is applicable and useful for both GPS pile drivers and non-GPS pile drivers. The piles come in varying lengths per the project specifications and are identified with different colors. CivDot can mark locations for 3,000 piles per day within 4 inches accuracy, ensuring the right pile is placed closer enough for the pile driver to pound. The CivDot takes the piles' design data, creates an optimized route, and marks the pile locations with spray paint. The operator can then install either colored flags, nails with whiskers, or stakes. Carrying out pile staging activity with CivDot increases the pile driving efficiency. CivDot has helped improve the survey time up to six times for our clients like Bechtel. Pre-Drilling Solar farms take up space. For example, a 220 MW (roughly 1,100 acres) takes up as much as 833 American football fields. With the solar market booming, many new projects are challenged by difficult site terrains made of rocky, dense, and full of caliche soils. Pre-drilling becomes a necessary step. Pre-drilling is the process of drilling through rocks and hard soil to replace them with softer material that is easy to pound through for piling. It’s important to have an accurate layout of drilling locations so that the crews can work more efficiently. CivDot+ has an accuracy of 3/100’ (8 mm) and can pin-point up to 1,200 points per day. Ground Screws An alternative for drilling and piling when the terrain is harder. Ground screws are used to cut through the most challenging soil conditions. It requires a precise layout like piling. MV Lines Medium-voltage (MV) lines are installed to connect the solar panels and distribute the electricity generated. Proper design, installation, and maintenance of MV lines are essential to maximize the performance and reliability of solar energy systems. CivDot can survey and lay out the location for trenching for MV lines. It can help prepare a real-scale blueprint with dashes for MV lines. Fencing Fencing around solar farms serves multiple purposes, from security and safety to ecological conservation. Civ Robotics’ robots help by efficiently locating points for fencing. The robots can accurately mark out the perimeter of the project, ensuring that the fence is properly placed without any gaps or overlaps. Battery Storage Battery storage in solar farms refers to the use of rechargeable batteries to store excess energy generated by solar panels. This stored energy can then be used during peak demand or when there is less sunlight, making the solar farm more efficient and reliable. Battery storage is placed on a leveled concrete slab, which requires creating a new foundation or framework. Civ Robotics shows construction workers where to cast the concrete for battery storage. jobs.title: Earthworks
jobs.description: Earthworks Trenching Trenching is the process of digging narrow channels or trenches in the ground for diverse purposes, such as installing underground utilities, laying cables, pipes, or conduits, and creating drainage systems. Civ Robotics’ autonomous surveying solution draws trench lines in realscale across various project types, job sites, and challenging environments. It offers a faster, safer, more accurate, and cost-effective solution. It helps measure the ground elevation and guides the field crew on how deep to dig. TOPO Topo or topographic surveying is the measurement and mapping of the physical features and contours of the land surface. Topo helps provide detailed information about the terrain, such as elevation changes and slopes. Civ Robots measure the ground elevation at every coordinate they mark. In addition, users can also enable Civ Robots to continuously measure the ground at predefined time and distance while in motion. Cut & Fill Cut and fill refers to the process of excavating earth material (cut) from one area of a site and using it to fill (fill) another area to achieve desired grades, slopes, or contours. Civ Robots help with grade checking using delta elevation feature. Grade Checking Grade checking is the process of ensuring the vertical accuracy of the finished surface grades or elevations according to design specifications. CivDot helps in grade checking with elevation differences. jobs.title: Ground Improvements
jobs.description: Ground Improvements Dynamic Compaction Commonly used in construction to prepare the ground for foundations, roadways, and other structures, dynamic compaction is a technique that densifies soils. It involves filling materials by dropping a heavy weight from a significant height. The process reduces the void in the soil, leading to increased density, strength, and stiffness. Civ Robotics’ autonomous robots are useful in accurately laying out where to drop heavy weights in a common pattern of either 5’ by 5’ or 10’ by 10’ Wick Drain Ground improvement technique used to provide a short path for water to escape from soil. Wick drains are narrow, perforated, corrugated plastic or synthetic strips wrapped in a geotextile fabric. Civ Robotics’ precision in land surveying and layout is invaluable in planning and executing the installation of 10,000 to 100,000 wick drains, ensuring the ground improvement process is conducted efficiently and accurately. Columns A technique used to enhance the strength, stiffness, and overall performance of soil. Particularly useful in areas with compressible soil conditions, columns improve the load-bearing capacity of the ground and reduce settlement. Some examples of columns include Controlled modulus columns, Stone columns, and bi-modulus columns. Civ Robotics’ technology helps in the planning and installation of columns by offering millimeter-level accuracy in land surveying and layout coordinates. Precise placement of columns is crucial for improving soil stability and support for future constructions.
